title: Surjectivity descends to a finite stage of a limit
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set and $(S_i,f_{ii'})$ an inverse system of schemes [def-pc-scheme] over $I$ with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism], with limit $S=\varprojlim_iS_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Let $0\in I$ and let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a morphism of schemes over $S_0$, where $S_0$, $X_0$, $Y_0$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For $i\ge0$ let $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ be the base change of $f_0$ to $S_i$ and $f:X\to Y$ its base change to $S$ (fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]). If $f$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] and $f_0$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], then $f_i$ is surjective for some $i\ge0$ (Stacks Limits, Lemma 07RR).

source.place: Lemma Tag 07RR (lemma-descend-surjective, line 2069), in Situation Tag 081D (situation-descent-property, line 1739); its proof: $f_0$ is of finite presentation, so $E=f_0(X_0)$ is constructible (Chevalley, Morphisms Lemma Tag 054J); the image of $f_i$ is the inverse image of $E$ in $Y_i$; $Y\to Y_0$ maps into $E$, so Limits Lemma Tag 05F4 (lemma-limit-contained-in-constructible) gives $i$ with $Y_i\to Y_0$ mapping into $E$

proof.text: *Step 1 (the image $E$ of $f_0$ is constructible).* Since $X_0$ is quasi-compact and $Y_0$ is quasi-separated, $f_0$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (1); it is locally of finite presentation by hypothesis, and $Y_0$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Hence by [lem-weil-pbc-chevalley-constructible-image] (clause $C=X_0$) the set $E=f_0(X_0)$ is a constructible subset of $Y_0$ [def-weil-constructible-subset]. (Stacks says '$f_0$ is of finite presentation'; only quasi-compactness of $f_0$ and the hypotheses on $Y_0$ enter Chevalley's theorem.)

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 07RR (lemma-descend-surjective, line 2069): 'The morphism $f_0$ is of finite presentation. Hence $E=f_0(X_0)$ is a constructible subset of $Y_0$, see Morphisms, Lemma 054J'

proof.text: *Step 2 (the base change image, directly).* For any g:T→S₀, identify the left map of Over.pullback(g).map(f₀) with pullback.map(X₀.hom,g,Y₀.hom,g,f₀.left,id_T,id_S₀). The identity map of S₀ is a monomorphism. Mathlib Scheme.Pullback.range_map computes its range as q_T⁻¹(range(f₀.left)) intersected with the inverse image of range(id_T), hence simply q_T⁻¹(E). This is the base-change-image identity of [lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image], obtained without a separate cartesian-square-pasting argument.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 07RR (lemma-descend-surjective, line 2069): 'we see that the image of $f_i$ is the inverse image of $E$ in $Y_i$' (Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 01S1, line 1489: $q^{-1}(f(Z))=f_{S'}(p^{-1}(Z))$)

proof.text: *Step 3 ($Y\to Y_0$ maps into $E$).* Since $f$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], Step 2 for $T=S$ gives $Y=f(X)=q_S^{-1}(E)$, i.e. $q_S(Y)\subseteq E$ for the projection $q_S:Y=Y_0\times_{S_0}S\to Y_0$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 07RR (lemma-descend-surjective, line 2069): 'Moreover, we know that $Y\to Y_0$ maps into $E$'

proof.text: *Step 4 (the upper-tail base change diagram).* Let J={i:I | i₀≤i}, with initial element j₀=i₀. It is directed: a common upper bound of two elements is still above i₀. The functor Jᵒᵖ→Over(op i₀) sending j to its transition arrow is fully faithful by thinness and essentially surjective by reading the source of an arrow; hence it is an equivalence. Whisker baseChangeDiagram D Y₀.hom and baseChangeCone D c Y₀.hom by this functor. By isLimitBaseChangeCone ([lem-weil-pbc-scheme-over-limit]) and invariance of limits under equivalence, this is a limiting cone. Its objects are qcqs and its transitions affine by the existing baseChangeDiagram compactSpace, quasiSeparatedSpace and affine-transition instances, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence].

source.place: Situation Tag 081D (situation-descent-property, line 1739) and Lemma Tag 01YZ (lemma-scheme-over-limit); the source applies Lemma Tag 05F4, stated in Situation Tag 086P (situation-descent, line 388: qcqs schemes, affine transition morphisms), to the system $(Y_i)$ without comment

proof.text: *Step 5 (constructible containment at a stage).* At j₀ let q₀ be the projection from Y₀×_{S₀}S₀ to Y₀; it is the canonical isomorphism. Transport E by q₀⁻¹ (the Lean proof uses Scheme.Hom.isConstructible_preimage). The equality baseChangeCone_π_app_fst proves that the image of the limit projection lies in q₀⁻¹(E). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-limit-contained-in-constructible] to the whiskered diagram at j₀. Choose its supplied stage j and specialize eventual containment at j itself. The equality baseChangeDiagram_map_fst turns this containment into range(q_j)⊆E.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 07RR (lemma-descend-surjective, line 2069): 'Hence we win by Lemma 05F4 (lemma-limit-contained-in-constructible, line 530)'

proof.text: *Step 6 (conclusion).* Let $i=i_1$. By Step 2 and Step 5, $f_i(X_i)=q_{S_i}^{-1}(E)=Y_i$, so $f_i$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] (and so is $f_{i'}$ for every $i'\ge i_1$).

The separate cartesian-square-pasting step is unnecessary.

Step 1: f_0 quasi-compact (qcqs-morphism-permanence (1)), so E = f_0(X_0) is constructible by Chevalley (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-chevalley-constructible-image = Scheme.Hom.isConstructible_image, FinitePresentation.lean:165, @[stacks 054J], with IsConstructible.univ). Step 2: X_T -> Y_T is a fibre product of f_0 and Y_T -> Y_0 by pasting (reviewed leaf lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting), for T = S_i or S. Step 3: image of f_T = inverse image of E (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image = Scheme.image_preimage_eq_of_isPullback, PullbackCarrier.lean:420; the identity in the proof of Morphisms 01S1). Step 4: surjectivity of f gives Y -> Y_0 into E. Step 5: Y = lim Y_i with affine transitions (lem-weil-pbc-scheme-over-limit, 01YZ) and Y_i qcqs (affine-morphism-permanence, qcqs-morphism-permanence (2)), the hypotheses of 05F4. Step 6: 05F4 (new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-limit-contained-in-constructible, stated for constructible E in Situation 086P; not in Mathlib, only the open case exists_map_eq_top). Step 7: conclusion. Statement kept; 05F3 not created (only cited in the source place of the 05F4 node, as part of Stacks' proof).
